idea-plugin.name: OXP - Open Extension Protocol
idea-plugin.description:
Run universal OXP extensions (.wasm components) inside any JetBrains IDE. One extension binary, every editor — write it once, ship it to IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, RustRover, CLion, DataGrip, and VS Code and Neovim.

What is OXP?

OXP (Open Extension Protocol) is an open spec for editor extensions distributed as sandboxed WebAssembly components (WASI Preview 2). The same .oxp bundle runs unchanged in every OXP-compatible host. This plugin is the JetBrains host.

Features

  • Install from URL — paste any https://…/extension.oxp (or file://); the bundle is downloaded, sha256- verified, signature-checked, cached, and loaded into a sandboxed wasm runtime (Rust + wasmtime).
  • Capability-based permissions — every extension declares the capabilities it needs (net.fetch, fs.read, shell.exec, …). You approve them before activation. Cancel = no install.
  • In-IDE rendering — extensions draw their UI in the OXP tool window via the oxp:ui/v1 interface (declarative component tree or sandboxed webview). No native code, no plugin classloader pollution.
  • Live dev sessions — start an Extension Development Host with Tools → OXP → Start Dev Session (EDH) and the extension hot-reloads on every save of an oxp dev server.
  • Deterministic bundles — every published .oxp is reproducible (sorted, mtime-stripped tar + zstd) and signed with Ed25519. The digest in the marketplace matches the bytes you load.

Quick start

  1. Open Tools → OXP → Install OXP Bundle… and paste the URL of any .oxp bundle, or run oxp install @publisher/slug from your terminal.
  2. Approve the requested capabilities.
  3. Open the OXP tool window (right side bar). Your installed extensions appear there — click one to load its UI.

Building your own extension

Install the CLI (npm i -g @oxprotocol/cli), then:

oxp create my-ext   # scaffold (templates: html, tree, rust, code)
cd my-ext
oxp dev             # live reload in your running IDE
oxp pack            # build a signed .oxp
oxp publish         # ship to https://oxp.sh

Security

  • Sandboxed: extensions have no ambient authority. No FS, network, or process access without an explicit granted capability.
  • Verified: sha256 + Ed25519 signature on every install.
  • Allowlisted: net.fetch can be scoped to specific hosts; fs.read to specific paths.
  • No native code: every extension is a .wasm component.

Links

  • Specification — oxp.sh/spec
  • CLI & SDK — npmjs.com/@oxprotocol/cli
  • Source — github.com/oxprotocol/oxp
  • Issues — github.com/oxprotocol/oxp/issues

idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.x — OXP Lens & Switchboard

  • OXP Lens Switchboard — a management panel that lists all installed extensions with toggle switches. Toggle ON → the extension gets its own native JetBrains tool window (LEFT anchor). Toggle OFF → it disappears instantly. No reload required.
  • Native tool windows per extension — each enabled extension registers as an independent sidebar panel at the same level as Project, Structure, and Git views.
  • Pop-out floating windows — click ↗ on any extension row to open it as a full floating window for maximum screen real estate.
  • Persistent state — toggle preferences survive IDE restarts. Previously visible extensions reopen automatically on project load.
  • OXP Dev redesign — friendlier idle and error states, soft purple badge instead of the old dark-red warning.
  • Shared JCEF browser factory — bridge wiring is now DRY; both the Switchboard tool windows and the Installed tab use the same injection path.
  • New OXP brand icon across all tool windows and marketplace.

0.3.0

  • Extension list UI improvements and auto-open on CLI install.

0.2.0

  • Installed tab, ui-v1 JCEF rendering, auto-open on oxp install.

0.1.0

  • Initial release — Wasmtime runtime, shared install store, live-reload dev sessions.
